No, that's not right, and it matters for your design.

A model has no memory between conversations. Each time you call it, it sees only the text you send in that call, and it writes a reply from that text plus what it learned in training. Training happened before any student talked to it, so a chat last week doesn't change the model. It's like a car's ECU with no data logger. It reacts to the sensor readings it gets right now, and nothing from last week's drive is there unless something recorded it and feeds it back in.

It's tempting to think otherwise because chatbots *feel* like they remember. Inside one conversation, the app resends the whole transcript each turn, so the model appears to keep track. Some products also add a saved-memory feature. That's extra machinery around the model, not the model itself.

For your assistant, remembering a student's training status means you build it:

- Save the facts you care about (for example "completed laser cutter training on Oct 3") in a file or database, keyed by student.
- At the start of a session, load that student's record.
- Put the relevant part into the text you send to the model.

That is the "what to save between sessions" decision in your mission, and it's the next topic on your list.

Quick check: if a student chats Monday and returns Friday, and your code sends only Friday's message, what does the model know about Monday?

I can write a short hands-on lesson on this where you run it and see it happen, if you want one.
